storyNotes.originalText: Abraham sent his servant back to his home country to find a WIFE for Isaac from his relatives.
storyNotes.cleanText: Abraham sent his servant back to his home country to find a wife for Isaac from his relatives.

storyNotes.originalText: At the well, the servant prayed, “May the woman you’ve chosen offer to bring WATER to my camels.”
storyNotes.cleanText: At the well, the servant prayed, “May the woman you’ve chosen offer to bring water to my camels.”

storyNotes.originalText: When the servant asked her for a drink, Rebekah also brought WATER to his camels.
storyNotes.cleanText: When the servant asked her for a drink, Rebekah also brought water to his camels.

storyNotes.originalText: The servant PRAISED God for answering his prayer and giving him success on his mission.
storyNotes.cleanText: The servant praised God for answering his prayer and giving him success on his mission.

storyNotes.originalText: The servant TOLD Rebekah’s father Bethuel and brother Laban all that God had done.
storyNotes.cleanText: The servant told Rebekah’s father Bethuel and brother Laban all that God had done.

storyNotes.originalText: Rebekah agreed to leave with the servant. Her father and brother gave her their BLESSING.
storyNotes.cleanText: Rebekah agreed to leave with the servant. Her father and brother gave her their blessing.

storyNotes.originalText: Isaac saw them as they arrived home. He MARRIED Rebekah and loved her.
storyNotes.cleanText: Isaac saw them as they arrived home. He married Rebekah and loved her.

questions.question: Do you remember that baby's name?
Where did he send the servant?
questions.answer: To his own country, where his relatives lived.

questions.question: What had God promised Abraham?
questions.answer: To grow his family into a great nation.

questions.question: What is a well?
questions.answer: A deep hole in the ground filled with water.

questions.question: How could he know which girl would be a good fit for Isaac?
questions.notes: Original open/rhetorical teaching question without a printed parenthetical answer; not automatically used on stand-alone worksheets.

questions.question: What did he do instead?
What special words was he waiting to hear?
questions.answer: I’ll get some for your camels, too.

questions.question: What was her name?
What did Rebekah say?
questions.answer: Yes. I'll get some for your camels, too!

questions.question: What did that mean?
questions.answer: Rebekah was the girl God had chosen for Isaac.

questions.question: At this point, did Rebekah know what was going on?
So what did Eliezer do after God made his search a smashing success?
questions.notes: Printed answer immediately follows question in running prose (not in parentheses).

questions.question: What did the servant have to say to Rebekah’s brother and father?
questions.notes: Original open/rhetorical teaching question without a printed parenthetical answer; not automatically used on stand-alone worksheets.

questions.question: What was the name of Rebekah's brother?
What do you think he wanted to tell Laban?
What did Rebekah's father Bethuel and brother Laban say after hearing about God’s amazingly quick answer to Eliezer’s prayer?
questions.answer: The Lord God has done this.

questions.question: What did he give?
What did she say?
What did they ask God to do?
As he did, what did he happen to see?
questions.answer: Abraham’s servant and Rebekah riding into town on their camels!

questions.question: After meeting, what did Isaac and Rebekah do?
What does the Bible say about Isaac's feelings for Rebekah?
So, how does the story of Isaac and Rebekah teach us, strengthen us, encourage us, or give us hope?
questions.notes: Original open/rhetorical teaching question without a printed parenthetical answer; not automatically used on stand-alone worksheets.

questions.question: What is prayer?
What does this tell us about praying?
Why?
questions.notes: Printed answer immediately follows question in running prose (not in parentheses).

questions.question: What did Jesus do to bless the whole world?
questions.answer: Died for our sins, rose from the dead.

questions.question: What did she do?
What did Abraham send his servant Eliezer to do?
Why was Abraham certain the servant would be successful?
questions.answer: God promised to grow his family into a great nation

questions.question: What did the servant pray?
questions.answer: Let the woman you've chosen for Isaac say, "I'll get water for your camels, too."

questions.question: Who came to the well before the servant finished praying?
When the servant asked for a drink, what did Rebekah say?
questions.answer: I'll get some water for your camels, too

questions.question: What did the servant give to Rebekah?
Who were Bethuel and Laban?
When the servant told Bethuel and Laban what happened, what did they say?
questions.answer: The Lord has done this, let Rebekah marry Isaac

questions.question: Where was Isaac when Rebekah and the servant returned?
What did Isaac do after meeting Rebekah? How did he feel about her?
questions.answer: He married her and loved her

facts.statement: Abraham sent his servant to find a wife for Isaac among relatives.
Abraham wanted Isaac to marry a woman from Canaan.
Eliezer took ten camels on the journey to find a wife for Isaac.
Eliezer stopped to pray  at the bottom of a well.
Eliezer asked God for a woman who would water his camels.
Rebekah offered water to Eliezer and his camels.
Rebekah demanded to be paid before watering the camels.
Eliezer praised God after his prayer was answered.
Laban refused to welcome Abraham’s servant into his home.
Rebekah’s father was Bethuel, and her brother was Laban.
Rebekah agreed to leave home with Abraham’s servant.
Isaac first met Rebekah beside the well.
Isaac married Rebekah and loved her.

clues.text: I asked my trusted servant to find a wife for my son Isaac.
I prayed beside a well and asked God to guide me in finding Isaac’s wife.
I gave a traveler water and offered to water his camels too.
My sister Rebekah met Abraham’s servant at the well.
My father sent a servant to find me a wife, and I married Rebekah.
